newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novus, Energy Equity up on well report.
newsitem.headline: Novus, Energy Equity up on well report.

text.p: Shares of oil companies Novus Petroleum NL and Energy Equity Corp Ltd rose on Monday after Novus released a progress report on the Singa-1 well on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
At 11.10 a.m (0110 GMT), Novus shares were 12 cents higher at A$4.35 while Energy Equity shares were 10 cents up at A$1.44.

In the report, Novus said the well entered the top of main reservoir target at 3635 metres on May 9. At this time there was an influx of fluid into the well known as a "kick" which Novus said was a common ocurence that did not present any danger to safety or the integrity of the well.
"The gas was confirmed at the surface as hydrocarbon gas. After the kick was experienced the mud weight was increased and the well quickly stabilised," the company said.
The Singa prospect is located 10 km south of the Belimbing oil field, which is part of the prolific Limau oil trend in South Sumatra.
Energy Equity is the operator of the well and has a 20 percent stake. The other partners are Novus with 15 percent, Amerada Hess Corp with 50 percent and Coparex International SA with 15 percent.
"This is obviously a very good result as it proves the presence of some gas in the top of the main reservoir target," said Novus technical director Phil Vingoe.
Vingoe said the next step for the venturers was to drill ahead and further evaluate the target zone.
"While the results to date are very encouraging, it is still early days and we await further results before we can determine the significance of the hydrocarbons encountered," he said.
The company said the forward programme was to resume drilling the Batu Raja reservoir with the subsequent work programme dependent on the results of that drilling and evaluation.
"This and further evaluation will be required to determine the commercial significance, if any, of this result." Novus said.
